title_core.description: The plain job noun a recruiter would search for, e.g. 'backend engineer'

location.description: As the posting states it, e.g. 'London, UK (hybrid)'

eligibility.description: Rules the candidate must meet that a résumé line can't prove: work authorisation, 'no visa sponsorship', 'must be based in Ontario', clearance, required languages. Reported, not written onto the résumé.

asks.description: Every requirement and responsibility, as short phrases. Usually 12-35 items.

id.description: M1, M2... for must-haves; N1... for nice-to-haves; R1... for responsibilities

alts.description: Plain phrases a resume would use when it shows this ask (not the posting's wording)

claimable.description: false when nothing in the candidate's sources supports it: an honest gap

note.description: Why it is a gap, or what the user confirmed

hard_terms.description: Exact names an ATS keyword search would use: tools, languages, platforms, products, methods with proper names, certifications, licences, degrees.

term.description: Spelled exactly as the posting spells it

variants.description: Other spellings of the same thing, e.g. 'K8s' for 'Kubernetes'

alternatives.description: Other tools that meet the same requirement ('TensorFlow' for 'PyTorch or TensorFlow'). Any one counts as present.

do_not_echo.description: Posting prose that must not be copied into the resume: mission lines, adjectives, stock phrases
